title: The HAVING Clause
flavorText: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Never use WHERE on an aggregate.
narrative: You need categories where the total stock count exceeds 500 — but only after grouping.
schemaSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL, stock INTEGER NOT NULL);
seedSql: INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Datapad','Electronics',299.99,45),(2,'Power Cell','Electronics',19.99,200),(3,'Steel Cable','Hardware',8.50,500),(4,'Logic Board','Electronics',89.99,30),(5,'Ceramic Fuse','Hardware',2.25,1000),(6,'Optic Lens','Optics',149.99,15),(7,'Servo Motor','Robotics',55.00,80),(8,'Pressure Valve','Hardware',12.75,300);
task: Find categories where the total stock (SUM of stock) is greater than 500. Order by total_stock descending.

hints.text: HAVING filters after GROUP BY. Syntax: GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(stock) > 500
SELECT category, SUM(stock) AS total_stock FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(stock) > 500 ORDER BY total_stock DESC;
SELECT category, SUM(stock) AS total_stock FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(stock) > 500 ORDER BY total_stock DESC;
